answer:
Here is what I would raise at your check-up, most urgent first. Your records run to mid-October 2026.

1. Your stool test (FIT) from 4 November 2025 was positive. I can't find a colonoscopy or any other follow-up test after it. A positive FIT normally needs a colonoscopy, so please ask about this first, and book one if it has not happened.

2. Your diabetes check is due. Your last HbA1c was 6.9% on 16 February 2026, which is more than eight months ago. It is usually checked every three to six months.

3. Your diabetes medicines changed. Metformin ended in April 2024, and Jardiance was prescribed in February 2025. Your HbA1c was 7.4% in July 2024 and 8.3% in January 2025, in the gap. Your records do not say why, so ask whether there was a break in treatment.

4. Your cholesterol was high before you started the statin. Your LDL was 131 mg/dL on 18 February 2025, two days before atorvastatin was prescribed. There is no cholesterol test in your records since then, so ask about a repeat lipid panel.

5. There is no urine albumin test in your records. For people with type 2 diabetes this is usually checked once a year. It may have been done elsewhere, so ask.

6. No vaccines are recorded for you. If you have had some, ask your doctor to add them. If not, ask which ones are due at your age.

7. Nothing to worry about from your July 2025 scan. The CT angiogram found no pulmonary embolism (a blood clot in the lung), and that condition is recorded as ruled out. Your chest wall pain is recorded as resolved.

Your kidney results from February 2026 (creatinine 0.88 mg/dL, eGFR 69) and your potassium (4.3 mmol/L) are within the normal range.
short: Positive FIT in November 2025 with no follow-up colonoscopy recorded. HbA1c is overdue (last 6.9% in February 2026). LDL was 131 mg/dL before a statin, with no repeat lipid test since. Diabetes medicines show a gap in 2024-25. No urine albumin test or vaccines are recorded.
